Chapter 150: Music Platforms are All Scams

"Let's go!"

After recording the two songs, Bian Guanyue came out, skipping and hopping.

Chen Guiliang shook hands with Li Jian and Li Chunsheng. "Goodbye, you two. Hope we can work together again next time."

Li Jian offered a reminder. "I know you're doing this to promote Xiaonei, so you might not care much about the profit from the songs themselves. But when you're choosing a platform to upload them to, you should read their user agreements carefully."

Chen Guiliang instantly understood what he meant. "Thanks for the reminder!"

After getting on the bus with Bian Guanyue, Chen Guiliang called Senior Sister Ao. "Big Boss, could you please ask someone with a law degree to come to the company? They don't need to be brilliant, just good enough to spot loopholes in online agreements."

"That's easy," Ao Yanchen reminded him. "Just pay them a little something. Don't try to fob them off with a barbecue again."

"No problem, haha," Chen Guiliang laughed awkwardly.

After Chen Guiliang hung up, Bian Guanyue asked, "Is there something wrong with those music platforms?"

Chen Guiliang nodded. "Li Jian just gave us a heads-up. Otherwise, we might have fallen into a trap. Things have been going too smoothly recently, which has lowered my guard. I didn't even think about that."

By the time the two returned to the company, the senior that Ao Yanchen had invited was already there.

Ao Yanchen made the introduction. "This is Senior Xiao Shaohui from the law department."

"Hello, Senior Xiao."

"Haha, CEO Chen, I've heard so much about you. What do you need my help with?"

"Take a look at Fenbei Net's user agreement first."

Fenbei Net was known as the cradle of online singers. A whole bunch of online songs, including "Mouse Loves Rice," had become popular there.

Senior Xiao Shaohui only looked at it for a few minutes before pointing to the user agreement and saying:

"The key parts are all ambiguous clauses. For example, here: 'The platform has the right to use user content for commercial cooperative projects.' What kind of commercial cooperative projects? It doesn't specify the scope at all. Once you upload a song, the website can use it for anything!"

"And here, it only says 'the user retains the copyright,' but does the user retain the commercial rights? It's not mentioned at all. If a lawsuit ever happens, it'll be a complete mess. Plus, there's no specific legislation right now. Even if the website commits copyright infringement in the future, the court will probably just order them to pay a small compensation."

"And here, the description is also too vague..."

Chen Guiliang followed Senior Xiao's finger, carefully reading through several ambiguous descriptions. "Damn, this Fenbei Net is a real shark."

It was because of these ambiguous clauses that, even when an online song's ringtone revenue exceeded a hundred million, it had nothing to do with the songwriters or singers.

The hundred million in revenue belonged to them!

A platform with a bit of a conscience might give you one or two million.

A truly disgusting platform would just give you a few hundred thousand and send you on your way.

It's useless to sue. At most, the judge will take pity on you and order the infringing party to compensate you two or three hundred thousand.

Even more ridiculous, an online singer might upload their song to multiple platforms simultaneously. Then all those music platforms would claim they owned the copyright and sue each other for infringement.

It was like an honest person getting robbed, and the robbers running to the authorities to report that the other robbers had stolen their money.

Even the judges would be baffled. It was a complete and utter mess.

Senior Xiao read through the user agreements of those websites one by one and finally found a legitimate one. "This 9tian Music is not bad. It clearly states that the platform only provides a distribution channel and will not automatically obtain commercial development rights. If a song is used for ringtones, film, or television, a supplementary agreement must be signed with the author and royalties paid."

"Write that down," Chen Guiliang said to Xie Yang.

Senior Xiao looked at a few more websites and said again, "QQ Music is also very legitimate."

Although Tencent was disgusting, they were decent in this respect.

Senior Xiao spent half an hour reading the user agreements of more than twenty platforms. He got faster and faster as he went on, heading straight for the ambiguous clauses.

In the end, only 9tian Music and QQ Music were considered legitimate.

All the others were fucking bastards!

Bian Guanyue said with lingering fear, "I spent so much time finding all these music platforms, and it turns out they're all booby-trapped. It's a good thing someone reminded us today."

"Haha, it's alright. I almost fell for it too," Chen Guiliang comforted her.

What Chen Guiliang was thinking was: Once the venture capital funds arrive, I'm definitely setting up a legal department.

Immediately, Chen Guiliang had Xie Yang upload "The Wind Rises" to 9tian Music and QQ Music.

Next, he embedded "The Wind Rises" into the story relay event page with the three pictures.

The song Bian Guanyue had composed on her own, called "The Bicycle Wind," was also recorded this time and uploaded to the music platforms by herself.

Leaning over the computer, Bian Guanyue waited for a few minutes. "Why is the download count still 0?"

Xie Yang, however, knew a little about computers. "Updating the front-end data in real-time puts a strain on the server. Especially for a music website with a huge number of downloads. They usually update once every two or three days, maybe even once a week."

"So you mean it will show 0 downloads for the next two or three days?" Bian Guanyue's enthusiasm for checking the stats instantly vanished.

Xie Yang said, "Not necessarily. For example, if it breaks ten thousand downloads in a short period of time, it might show ten thousand. It depends on how the website is configured."

Senior Xiao went to Ao Yanchen's office to get his payment.

Chen Guiliang went downstairs to get his bicycle and took Bian Guanyue for a leisurely ride around the campus on the weekend.

From time to time, people would recognize him.

But everyone was used to it by now. Only those who were relatively familiar with him would greet him. Others acted as if they didn't see him, but would instead steal a few more glances at Bian Guanyue.

"Wu Meng, come out and get some sun!"

Chen Guiliang stopped in front of the dormitory building and shouted towards the dorms. They had arranged this beforehand.

Before long, Wu Meng came out with a roommate and waved at them. "Hi, CEO Chen, Guan Guan!"

"We're going to Yuanmingyuan today," said Bian Guanyue.

Chen Guiliang said, "You guys should rent bikes too. We can all ride over together."

Four people, three bikes, heading north.

Bian Guanyue stretched out her hand as if trying to catch the wind. She really enjoyed riding on a bicycle now.

Wu Meng and her roommate rode behind them.

"Is that Chen Guiliang's girlfriend?"

"Yeah, my deskmate from high school."

"Sigh, looks like I don't stand a chance. All the handsome guys are taken."

"Hahaha. Chen Guiliang has a good friend named Xie Yang who also works at his company. I'll introduce you two someday."

"Is he handsome?"

"Um... passable, I guess."

The handsome Xie Sao Bang was currently slaving away at the company. He had to work overtime every weekend.

Or rather, he was even busier on weekends.

But he enjoyed it.

Whenever he had free time, he would read some professional books Chen Guiliang had borrowed, then seriously reflect on them, combining the knowledge with his own practical experience.

Some parts he only half-understood, so he would note them down first. Then he would find time to sneak into Peking University to audit classes, pretending to be a student, and ask those famous professors for advice.

Busy and fulfilling, he felt more and more that he had wasted his time in his last year of high school.

But occasionally, he also felt lonely and really wanted to find a girlfriend.

Using the excuse of going to the bathroom, Xie Yang strolled to the office next door.

Xu Fengyin was also working overtime there, and she had volunteered for it. The place she rented was old and small; she'd rather hang out at the company.

"Still drawing?" Xie Yang tossed his handsome hair.

Xu Fengyin was so startled she quickly grabbed her keyboard and pressed it down on her drawing, afraid that someone would see what she was drawing.

It was actually nothing much, just a little risqué.

Working overtime on a weekend drawing game skins, she could totally get paid for slacking off, taking occasional breaks to doodle something else.

Xie Yang glanced at the customer service staff on duty in the distance and said in a low voice, "Eating at the cafeteria every day is boring. How about we get some stir-fry for dinner tonight?"

As he spoke, he reached up to flick his hair again.

"Maybe next time." Xu Fengyin just wanted him to leave quickly.

She usually seemed quite cheerful, but she was actually a bit of a loner. Especially after getting obsessed with manga in middle school, she spent all her non-studying time reading and drawing manga, and her communication with friends and family grew less and less.
